docs.title: OSRSClient Public API
docs.text:
This site documents the public scripting / plugin API, exposed in two mirror forms:

  • C++ — srs::api::*, for plugins compiled against OSRSClient.lib. Headers live in OSRSClient/PluginAPI/API/. Plugins implement IScript (OSRSClient/PluginAPI/IScript.h) and call API methods, passing the ScriptContext& they receive in onLoad / pulse / onTick / onDraw.
  • Lua — srs.*, for .lua scripts loaded by the in-process Lua VM. Bindings live in OSRSClient/ScriptEngine/ScriptAPI.cpp. The host builds the ScriptContext internally; scripts just call srs.<module>.<method>(args).

The two forms are at feature parity — every method documented here is callable from both C++ and Lua. Differences in shape (where unavoidable, e.g. Lua lacks pointer semantics) are called out per-method.

Threading and spoofing contract

All action-firing methods (interact, attack, click, cast, …) route through Interact on the engine main thread with always-on input spoofing. There is no escape hatch — calling DoAction from the render thread crashes, and the spoofer is fail-closed (if it can't inject, the action drops).

docs.title: C++ — IScript
docs.text:
class IScript {
public:
    virtual const char* name() const = 0;
    virtual bool onLoad(const ScriptContext& ctx) = 0;
    virtual void onUnload() = 0;

    virtual void pulse  (const ScriptContext& ctx) {}  // per frame (~60Hz)
    virtual void onTick (const ScriptContext& ctx) {}  // per game tick (~600ms)
    virtual void onDraw (const ScriptContext& ctx) {}  // per frame, inside ImGui frame

    virtual void onSettingsChanged(const nlohmann::json& settings) {}
    virtual nlohmann::json schema() const { return {}; }
};

Plugins export CreateScript / DestroyScript functions and ship as DLLs in the plugins/ directory.

docs.title: Lua — callback registration
docs.text:
script.pulse(function() ... end)   -- per frame
script.onTick(function() ... end)  -- per game tick
script.draw(function() ... end)    -- per frame, inside ImGui frame

script.draw is the only callback where srs.draw.* calls are valid — the host guarantees a live ImGui frame for it. pulse and onTick do not.

docs.title: pulse vs onTick
docs.text:
Callback Cadence Use for pulse every rendered frame (~60 Hz) cheap state checks, per-frame visual work onTick every game tick (~600 ms) action firing, state-machine transitions

The server can only process one action per tick, so per-frame action firing is wasted work that the spoofer will throttle. Move action logic to onTick and use pulse only for checks.

docs.title: Example — minimal Lua script
docs.text:
-- Drop every shrimp the moment it lands in the backpack.
script.onTick(function()
    if srs.inventory.contains("Shrimps") then
        srs.inventory.dropAll("Shrimps")
    end
end)

script.draw(function()
    if srs.draw.beginAnchoredOverlay(
            "##fish-hud", 162, 32,
            srs.Corner.TopRight, -4, 4) then
        srs.draw.text("Caught: " .. srs.inventory.count("Shrimps"))
        srs.draw.endOverlay()
    end
end)

docs.title: Example — minimal C++ plugin
docs.text:
class FishingPlugin : public IScript {
public:
    const char* name() const override { return "Fishing"; }
    bool onLoad(const ScriptContext&) override { return true; }
    void onUnload() override {}

    void onTick(const ScriptContext& ctx) override {
        using namespace srs::api;
        if (Inventory::contains(ctx, "Shrimps")) {
            Inventory::dropAll(ctx, "Shrimps");
        }
    }

    void onDraw(const ScriptContext& ctx) override {
        using namespace srs::api;
        if (Drawing::beginAnchoredOverlay(ctx, "##fish-hud",
                                          162, 32,
                                          Drawing::Corner::TopRight,
                                          -4, 4)) {
            Drawing::text("Caught: " + std::to_string(
                Inventory::count(ctx, std::string("Shrimps"))));
            Drawing::endOverlay();
        }
    }
};

extern "C" __declspec(dllexport) IScript* CreateScript()  { return new FishingPlugin(); }
extern "C" __declspec(dllexport) void DestroyScript(IScript* s) { delete s; }

docs.title: Antiban
docs.text:
srs::api::Antiban / srs.antiban

Human-like timing + idle behavior. Designed for onTick:

C++Lua 
void onTick(const ScriptContext& ctx) override {
    using namespace srs::api;
    if (Antiban::shouldDelay(ctx))      return;
    if (Antiban::shouldMicroBreak())    return;
    if (workIsDone()) {
        Antiban::moveMouseRandomly(ctx);
        return;
    }
    performAction(ctx);
    Antiban::recordAction();
}

script.onTick(function()
    if srs.antiban.shouldDelay()      then return end
    if srs.antiban.shouldMicroBreak() then return end
    if workIsDone() then
        srs.antiban.moveMouseRandomly()
        return
    end
    performAction()
    srs.antiban.recordAction()
end)

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method C++ Lua Record an action timestamp Antiban::recordAction() srs.antiban.recordAction() Ms since last action Antiban::idleTimeMs() → int64 srs.antiban.idleTimeMs() → int Idle past threshold (default 5m) Antiban::isIdleTooLong(thresholdMs?) → bool srs.antiban.isIdleTooLong(thresholdMs?) → bool Probabilistic action-skip (default 5%) Antiban::shouldDelay(ctx, fatigue?) → bool srs.antiban.shouldDelay(fatigue?) → bool Probabilistic micro-break (default 0.1%) Antiban::shouldMicroBreak(prob?) → bool srs.antiban.shouldMicroBreak(prob?) → bool Drift mouse to random screen point Antiban::moveMouseRandomly(ctx) → bool srs.antiban.moveMouseRandomly() → bool Send mouse off-screen Antiban::moveMouseOffScreen(ctx) → bool srs.antiban.moveMouseOffScreen() → bool Total delays skipped Antiban::totalDelaysSkipped() → uint64 srs.antiban.totalDelaysSkipped() → int Total micro-breaks Antiban::totalMicroBreaks() → uint64 srs.antiban.totalMicroBreaks() → int Total random moves Antiban::totalRandomMoves() → uint64 srs.antiban.totalRandomMoves() → int

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• shouldDelay's fatigue argument is the per-call skip probability (0..1). Default 5%; pass higher values during long sessions to slow the script down.
  • shouldMicroBreak's default of 0.1 % at 60 Hz works out to roughly one break per ~16 seconds of polling.
  • moveMouseRandomly reads the live viewport size from Camera::state(); falls back to (1024, 768) if the camera hasn't initialized.
  • The three total* counters feed the debug panel readout.

docs.title: Area
docs.text:
srs::api::Area / srs.area

Player-position area-containment checks. 2D only — plane is ignored. Add a plane-aware overload when an actual use case appears.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Form C++ Lua Inside inclusive rect Area::isWithin(ctx, x1, y1, x2, y2) → bool srs.area.isWithin(x1, y1, x2, y2) → bool Within Chebyshev radius Area::isWithin(ctx, cx, cy, tilesAway) → bool srs.area.isWithin(cx, cy, tilesAway) → bool
  • Rect form — (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) are opposing corners. Either pair works (upper-left + lower-right, upper-right + lower-left, etc.) — internally min/max-ed against each axis.
  • Radius form — tilesAway is inclusive (player on the boundary counts as inside). tilesAway = 0 means "exactly on the tile".

Lua dispatches by arity: 4 args = rect, 3 args = radius.

docs.title: Deferred (not yet shipped)
docs.text:
• Per-item withdraw — bank slot widgets are dynamic children with scrollable layout; the rect-from-grid math doesn't apply. Needs per-slot widget rect resolved through the IfRender capture by index.
  • Per-item deposit — same dynamic-child problem on the inventory side when the bank is open ("Deposit-1" etc.).
  • Bank PIN entry — keypad slots A..J are randomized per session; each click target's digit must be read from the rendered widget at click time.

docs.title: Combat
docs.text:
srs::api::Combat / srs.combat

Combat-tab queries and toggles. Reads from VarpSystem; writes via Widget::click on the combat tab (group 593). Toggle methods are no-ops if already in the desired state.

Backed by RuneLite-confirmed varbits/varps:

Varp Meaning 300 Special-attack energy (0..1000, 100% = 1000) 301 Special-attack enabled flag (0/1) 172 Auto-retaliate (0 = on, 1 = off, inverted) 43 Attack-style index

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Spec energy (0..1000) Combat::specEnergy(ctx) → int32 srs.combat.specEnergy() → int Spec energy (0..100 %) Combat::specEnergyPct(ctx) → int32 srs.combat.specEnergyPct() → int Spec enabled flag Combat::isSpecEnabled(ctx) → bool srs.combat.isSpecEnabled() → bool Currently in combat Combat::isInCombat(ctx) → bool srs.combat.isInCombat() → bool Auto-retaliate on Combat::isAutoRetaliate(ctx) → bool srs.combat.isAutoRetaliate() → bool Toggle spec button Combat::toggleSpec(ctx) → bool srs.combat.toggleSpec() → bool Set attack style Combat::setAttackStyle(ctx, style) → bool srs.combat.setAttackStyle(style) → bool Set auto-retaliate Combat::setAutoRetaliate(ctx, on) → bool srs.combat.setAutoRetaliate(on) → bool

Auto-retaliate sense

The underlying varp is inverted (0 = on, 1 = off); isAutoRetaliate / setAutoRetaliate expose the natural sense (true = retaliate is on).

isInCombat follows the Microbot pattern (local player → NPC interact target OR NPC → local player interact target).

docs.title: Example
Drawing
docs.text:
srs::api::Drawing / srs.draw

Overlay drawing.

onDraw only

Only valid inside IScript::onDraw (C++) or script.draw(fn) (Lua). The host guarantees a live in-game ImGui frame there; calling from pulse / onTick will fault on builds where those paths run off-frame.

docs.title: Anchoring
docs.text:
Pin overlays to OSRS widgets so they follow tab switches and layout mode changes.

Method C++ Lua Live widget rect (cached) Drawing::widgetRect(ctx, g, c) → optional<Rect> srs.draw.widgetRect(g, c) → Rect \| nil Compute pinned screen position Drawing::anchorToWidget(ctx, g, c, corner, dx?, dy?, pivot?) → optional<Vec2> srs.draw.anchorToWidget(g, c, corner, dx?, dy?, pivot?) → Vec2 \| nil Evict cached rects Drawing::clearAnchorCache() srs.draw.clearAnchorCache()

Anchor miss policy

anchorToWidget / widgetRect return the last seen rect for that (group, child) pair when the widget isn't drawn this frame. This keeps overlays pinned through brief widget flicker (tab switches, loading frames). Call clearAnchorCache() on logout or layout mode change to evict.

docs.title: Window lifecycle
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Open overlay at pos Drawing::beginOverlay(name, pos, pivot=TopLeft, bgAlpha=0.55) → bool srs.draw.beginOverlay(name, pos, pivot?, bgAlpha?) → bool One-call: anchor + begin Drawing::beginAnchoredOverlay(ctx, name, g, c, corner, dx?, dy?, pivot?, bgAlpha?) → bool srs.draw.beginAnchoredOverlay(name, g, c, corner, dx?, dy?, pivot?, bgAlpha?) → bool Close overlay Drawing::endOverlay() srs.draw.endOverlay()

Pair every begin* that returns true with one endOverlay. beginAnchoredOverlay returns false when the widget has never been seen (no cached rect either); in that case do NOT call endOverlay.

C++ takes a pointer to mutate the value in place; Lua returns a (changed, newValue) tuple since it lacks pointer semantics.

Method C++ Lua Button button(label, size={0,0}) → bool srs.draw.button(label, size?) → bool Small button smallButton(label) → bool srs.draw.smallButton(label) → bool Checkbox checkbox(label, bool*) → bool (changed) srs.draw.checkbox(label, value) → (changed, newValue) Slider int sliderInt(label, int*, vMin, vMax) → bool srs.draw.sliderInt(label, value, vMin, vMax) → (changed, newValue) Slider float sliderFloat(label, float*, vMin, vMax) → bool srs.draw.sliderFloat(label, value, vMin, vMax) → (changed, newValue) Progress bar progressBar(fraction, size={-1,0}, overlay=nullptr) srs.draw.progressBar(fraction, size?, overlay?)

docs.title: Food
docs.text:
srs::api::Food / srs.food

Static metadata table for edible items + eatBest() helper that picks the highest-heal food currently in the backpack.

docs.title: GameObject
docs.text:
srs::api::GameObject / srs.gameobject

Query and interact with scene loc objects — game objects, walls, decorations, ground decorations. Distinct from NPCs and players.

Names come from the runtime LocType cache; entries with empty names are nameless decorations (still queryable by id).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua All locs (heavy) GameObject::all(ctx) → vector<GameObjectEntry> srs.gameobject.all() → table By id GameObject::byId(ctx, id) → vector<GameObjectEntry> srs.gameobject.byId(id) → table By name GameObject::byName(ctx, name) → vector<GameObjectEntry> srs.gameobject.byName(name) → table Nearest (any) GameObject::nearest(ctx) → optional<GameObjectEntry> srs.gameobject.nearest() → GameObjectEntry \| nil Nearest by name GameObject::nearestByName(ctx, name) → optional<GameObjectEntry> srs.gameobject.nearestByName(name) → GameObjectEntry \| nil Interact (target + action) GameObject::interact(ctx, target, action) → bool srs.gameobject.interact(target, action) → bool Find-nearest-and-interact GameObject::interactNearest(ctx, name, action) → bool srs.gameobject.interactNearest(name, action) → bool

byName / nearestByName are case- and whitespace-insensitive against the in-game display name (e.g. "Bank booth", "bankbooth", and "BANK_BOOTH" all hit the same target).

all() is heavy

all() returns every loc in every loaded scene (all 4 planes). Tens of thousands of rows in a typical city. Prefer the filtered helpers, or filter the result yourself.

docs.title: Example
GroundItem
docs.text:
srs::api::GroundItem / srs.grounditem

Read-only enumeration of dropped items in every loaded WorldInstance, all 4 planes. Distance helpers use Chebyshev tile distance from the local player.

docs.title: Example
MenuEntry
docs.text:
srs::api::MenuEntry / srs.menuEntry

Typed fluent builder over Interact::doActionRaw. Goes through the same spoof-then-DoAction path as every other facade — fail-closed if the spoofer can't inject.

Use this when you need raw control over MenuAction params (e.g. while RE'ing a new interaction type) without bypassing the input simulation contract.

Equivalent to Microbot's NewMenuEntry, minus the option/target text fields (those route through Interact::perform's higher-level path; this builder targets the raw MenuAction dispatch path).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
C++Lua 
using srs::api::MenuEntry;
MenuEntry()
    .worldX(10).worldY(20)
    .opcode(/*CC_OP*/ 57)
    .screen(450, 300)
    .fire(ctx);

local e = srs.menuEntry.new()
e:worldX(10):worldY(20)
 :opcode(srs.menuEntry.CC_OP)
 :screen(450, 300)
 :fire()

docs.text: Setter C++ signature Lua signature worldX(v) MenuEntry& worldX(int32) entry:worldX(v) → entry worldY(v) MenuEntry& worldY(int32) entry:worldY(v) → entry widget(g, c) MenuEntry& widget(int32, int32) entry:widget(g, c) → entry opcode(op) MenuEntry& opcode(int32) entry:opcode(op) → entry spawnIndex(v) MenuEntry& spawnIndex(int32) entry:spawnIndex(v) → entry subject(v) MenuEntry& subject(uint32) entry:subject(v) → entry screen(x, y) MenuEntry& screen(int32, int32) entry:screen(x, y) → entry fire() bool fire(ctx) entry:fire() → bool

docs.title: Field semantics
docs.text:
• worldX / worldY — primary param pair. For tile actions these are world tile coords; for inventory / widget actions, worldX is the slot/sub-id and worldY is the encoded widget id.
  • widget(g, c) — convenience that encodes (groupId, childId) into worldY = (group << 16) | child.
  • screen(x, y) — required. Pixel coords of the click target. The spoofer needs these to draw a plausible mouse trail. Sentinel (0, 0) causes the spoofer to skip and fail-closed.

docs.title: NPC
docs.text:
srs::api::Npc / srs.npc

Per-NPC actions. The target is an ActionTarget — usually obtained from the entity query API (entityQuery) or other facade returns. The ActionTarget carries the spawn index and world coords that DoAction needs.

All interact / attack / talkTo / bank calls route through Interact, which always spoofs mouse motion + click before DoAction (no escape hatch).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Generic interact Npc::interact(ctx, target, action) → bool srs.npc.interact(target, action) → bool Attack Npc::attack(ctx, target) → bool srs.npc.attack(target) → bool Talk-to Npc::talkTo(ctx, target) → bool srs.npc.talkTo(target) → bool Bank (banker NPCs) Npc::bank(ctx, target) → bool srs.npc.bank(target) → bool Still in world map Npc::isAlive(ctx, target) → bool srs.npc.isAlive(target) → bool

action is the exact menu-option string the game shows ("Attack", "Talk-to", "Bank", "Pickpocket", "Trade", "Steal-from", …).

isAlive semantics

isAlive is a host-side check that the NPC's NpcInstance is still present in the world hash map. After an NPC dies it lingers a few ticks playing the death animation, then despawns — once that happens isAlive returns false. Currently does not treat HP-0-but-still-rendering as "dead"; callers that need that (loot timing, drop tracking) should poll currentHp via the NPCs panel column or entity.npcById(...).

docs.title: ActionTarget method-call shortcuts (Lua)
docs.text:
The ActionTarget usertype exposes the same set as methods:

local npc = entity.nearestNpc()
if npc and npc:isAlive() then
    npc:attack()         -- == srs.npc.attack(npc)
    npc:talkTo()
    npc:bank()
    npc:interact("Pickpocket")
end

Player
docs.text:
srs::api::Player / srs.player

Local-player state. Thin wrappers over GameData getters. Each helper returns a sensible fallback (empty string / -1 / 0) instead of optional so Lua callers don't have to deal with a multi-return shape.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method C++ Lua World-tile position Player::position(ctx) → WorldTile srs.player.position() → WorldTile Display name Player::displayName(ctx) → string srs.player.displayName() → string Active animation id Player::animation(ctx) → int32 srs.player.animation() → int Carried weight (kg) Player::weight(ctx) → int32 srs.player.weight() → int Run energy Player::runEnergy(ctx) → int32 srs.player.runEnergy() → int Toggle run Player::toggleRunEnergy(ctx, on) → bool srs.player.toggleRunEnergy(on) → bool Idle ticks counter Player::idleTicks(ctx) → int32 srs.player.idleTicks() → int

docs.title: Detail
docs.text:
• position — returns {0, 0, 0} when GS or the player struct isn't resolved (pre-login). Callers that care about the difference should check World::getId(ctx) >= 0 first.
  • displayName — empty string pre-login. Resolved via WI-map (GS+0xCA40 → WorldInstance → PlayerSubMap.find(LocalPlayerIndex)) in patch 238+.
  • animation — current animation id from the active AnimSlot. -1 = idle.
  • weight — reads VarPlayer 169.
  • runEnergy — in 0..10000 range (raw network units; divide by 100 for the displayed percentage). -1 if GS isn't resolved.
  • idleTicks — number of consecutive game ticks the player's active animation has been -1. Reset to 0 the moment any non-idle animation plays. Maintained by GameData::onTick.

docs.title: Prayer
docs.text:
srs::api::Prayer / srs.prayer

Toggle prayers and read state. Backed by the prayer book widget (group 541) for clicks and per-prayer activation varbits for reads.

docs.text:

docs.title: Example
Projectiles
docs.text:
srs::api::Projectiles / srs.projectiles

Read-only enumeration of in-flight projectiles. The common case is "what's about to hit me and when" — use incoming() for that.

Cache ids

id is this client's spotanim/graphic cache id (cache group 0xD in the OSRS-OS3303-BWXF build). It does not directly equal RuneLite's ProjectileID enum — different cache revisions diverge by varying amounts. If you need RuneLite-style labels, build a per-build mapping table.

Time units

ticksUntilLanding is in game ticks (600 ms each, rounded up from the underlying ~30-frame-per-tick counter at GS+0x2154).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Any incoming projectile (cheap) Projectiles::isUnderFire(ctx) → bool srs.projectiles.isUnderFire() → bool Incoming list Projectiles::incoming(ctx) → vector<ProjectileEntry> srs.projectiles.incoming() → table Next-to-land Projectiles::next(ctx) → optional<ProjectileEntry> srs.projectiles.next() → table \| nil Ticks until next Projectiles::ticksUntilNext(ctx) → int32 srs.projectiles.ticksUntilNext() → int All projectiles scene-wide (heavier) Projectiles::all(ctx) → vector<ProjectileEntry> srs.projectiles.all() → table
  • isUnderFire is allocation-free — preferred for tight check-loops.
  • next is the lowest absoluteEndCycle.
  • ticksUntilNext returns -1 when nothing is in flight (single int compare instead of optional unwrap, for ranged-prayer flick logic).
  • all is heavier than incoming — walks the WI hashmap.

docs.title: Tab
docs.text:
srs::api::Tab / srs.tab

Authoritative source for "which sidebar tab is open right now", mirroring Microbot's Rs2Tab.

Tab state lives in VarClient at index TOPLEVEL_PANEL (171). Reading it is stricter than the open-iface map (which only says the inventory IfType is loaded, not that it's the active tab).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method C++ Lua Current tab enum Tab::current(ctx) → InterfaceTab srs.tab.current() → int Is given tab open Tab::isOpen(ctx, tab) → bool srs.tab.isOpen(tab) → bool Switch to tab Tab::switchTo(ctx, tab) → bool srs.tab.switchTo(tab) → bool Raw varc value Tab::rawIndex(ctx) → int32 srs.tab.rawIndex() → int AWT VK code for tab hotkey Tab::hotkeyVk(ctx, tab) → int srs.tab.hotkeyVk(tab) → int

docs.title: switchTo contract
docs.text:
1. If current(ctx) == tab → return true immediately (no-op).
  2. Read the AWT VK code from the player's STONE_*_KEY varbit for this tab. If bound, inject it as a press+release via the keyboard ring — closest to real player behavior.
  3. If no hotkey is bound (varbit unset / snapshot not warmed) or the keypress can't be delivered (pre-login, GS unresolved), fall back to a spoofed click on the chrome tab widget. The chrome (group, child) pair is resolved from the live display mode (Fixed=548 / ResizableClassic=161 / ResizableModern=164).

hotkeyVk returns 0 if unbound (or if the varbit snapshot hasn't refreshed yet). Useful for "Inventory tab bound to: F4" UI or gating switchTo.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
InterfaceTab (InterfaceTab / srs.tab.*):

Lua const Value Tab UNKNOWN -1 VarClient not ready / pre-login NOTHING_SELECTED 0 No tab (fullscreen interface up) COMBAT 1 Combat SKILLS 2 Skills QUESTS 3 Quests INVENTORY 4 Inventory EQUIPMENT 5 Equipment PRAYER 6 Prayer MAGIC 7 Magic CHAT_CHANNEL 8 Chat channel FRIENDS 9 Friends ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT 10 Account management LOGOUT 11 Logout SETTINGS 12 Settings EMOTES 13 Emotes MUSIC 14 Music

Raw varc values don't match enum

The underlying varc value is 0-based and DOES NOT match this enum's ordinal — see Tab.cpp::current() for the conversion. The raw values mirror Microbot's InterfaceTab.varcIntIndex (e.g. Combat=0, Inventory=3, AccMan=8, Friends=9, Logout=10). The value -1 means "no tab selected" (fullscreen interface up, or pre-login).

docs.title: Walk
docs.text:
srs::api::Walk / srs.walk

High-level navigation facade over PathExecutor. Handles pathfinding (local A* + DaxWalker fallback), multi-leg navigation, transport invocation, and stall recovery internally.

Plugins should call Walk::to(ctx, x, y) and then poll Walk::hasArrived each tick instead of reaching into ctx.pathExecutor directly.

All calls are safe no-ops (returning false / true depending on intent) when ctx.pathExecutor isn't wired (pre-init host).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Walk to tile Walk::to(ctx, x, y, useTransports=true) → bool srs.walk.to(x, y, useTransports?) → bool Stop walking Walk::cancel(ctx) srs.walk.cancel() Currently walking Walk::isMoving(ctx) → bool srs.walk.isMoving() → bool At goal Walk::hasArrived(ctx) → bool srs.walk.hasArrived() → bool
  • to returns false if the executor isn't available or refused to start the walk (already-arrived, identical goal, etc.).
  • useTransports = false forces a walk-only path (free accounts, missing quest reqs).
  • Plane is read from the player's current plane — there's no cross-plane API surface yet.
  • hasArrived returns true when no walk has been issued yet (or the executor got as close as PathExecutor::CLOSE_ENOUGH allows).

docs.title: Example
Widget
docs.text:
srs::api::Widget / srs.widget

Read-only inspection of the OSRS interface tree, plus a generic click. Widgets are identified by (groupId, childId) — matches RuneLite's WidgetID encoding.

docs.title: State / lookup
docs.text: Method C++ Lua IfTypeManager warmed up Widget::isReady(ctx) → bool srs.widget.isReady() → bool Find by (group, child) Widget::find(ctx, g, c) → optional<WidgetSnapshot> srs.widget.find(g, c) → WidgetSnapshot \| nil All in group Widget::group(ctx, g) → vector<WidgetSnapshot> srs.widget.group(g) → table Dynamic children Widget::dynamicChildren(ctx, g, c) → vector<WidgetSnapshot> srs.widget.dynamicChildren(g, c) → table RuneLite-style label Widget::label(g, c) → string srs.widget.label(g, c) → string

docs.title: Dynamic children
docs.text:
dynamicChildren enumerates the runtime-allocated IfTypes held in the parent's vector at IfType+0xB58. This is where inventory slots, bank items, dialogue options, etc. live; they don't appear in group() (which only walks the static Components array).

Each entry's dynIndex carries its array slot, parentGroupId/parentChildId point to (g, c), and text typically holds the option label or item-derived caption.

docs.title: label
docs.text:
Returns the most informative form available, in priority order:

  1. "Inventory.ITEMS" — exact InterfaceID nested constant
  2. "INVENTORY[0]" — group name + child index
  3. "149.0" — numeric fallback

docs.title: Visibility
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Interface rendering Widget::isOpen(ctx, g) → bool srs.widget.isOpen(g) → bool Drawn last frame Widget::isVisible(ctx, g, c) → bool srs.widget.isVisible(g, c) → bool Hidden (or ancestor hidden) Widget::isHidden(ctx, g, c) → bool srs.widget.isHidden(g, c) → bool

isVisible returns true iff the engine actually drew the widget last frame (hook-snapshot path). The renderer skips any widget whose own or any ancestor's Hidden flag is set, so this matches RuneLite's recursive Widget.isHidden() semantics for free.

Defaults on lookup-miss mirror the Java helpers exactly:

  • isVisible(g, c) → false when widget can't be found
  • isHidden(g, c) → true when widget can't be found

docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Hit-test screen point Widget::atPoint(ctx, sx, sy) → optional<WidgetSnapshot> srs.widget.atPoint(sx, sy) → WidgetSnapshot \| nil Currently hovered Widget::hovered(ctx) → optional<WidgetSnapshot> srs.widget.hovered() → WidgetSnapshot \| nil

Rect fields are absolute screen coords for these two methods.

docs.title: Click
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Click action Widget::click(ctx, g, c, action) → bool srs.widget.click(g, c, action) → bool

Click a named action on a widget. Resolves the widget's absolute screen rect via the live IfRender capture, picks a random point in the rect, and routes through Interact (always-on spoof + DoAction).

For inventory slots prefer Inventory::interact — same mechanism, narrower API.

docs.title: World
docs.text:
srs::api::World / srs.world

Current world / server number.

The world int (e.g. 302, 398) is stored in the GS struct at GameSDK::Offsets::GlobalState::WorldId (= 0x321C). This API just wraps GameData::worldId() so plugins / Lua can read it without touching memory directly.
